reason: The text contains three actively named characters in the narrative: Moses (מֹשֶׁה), who is called to become the prophet and deliverer of Israel; Jethro (יִתְרוֹ), explicitly identified as 'priest of Midian' (כֹּהֵן מִדְיָן), a position of religious authority and leadership; and God (יְהוָה/אֱלֹהִים), the supreme authority. Additionally, referenced named figures (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Pharaoh) are all patriarchs or rulers. There are no named individuals of ordinary status—all named characters possess positions of authority or leadership.
